item.title: backlog list has no --priority filter — users cannot quickly see items by priority tier
item.intent: Users must be able to run 'backlog list --priority must' and see only must-priority items, completing the filter set alongside --status, --type, and --ready.
item.description: cmd_backlog_list supports --status, --type, and --ready filters but has no --priority flag. The most common pre-sprint question for scoped runs is 'what are all my must items?' Currently answered only by scanning the PRI column. A --priority filter would complete the filter set and mirror the auto p0/p1/p2 priority model.
steps: In cmd_backlog_list(), add local filter_priority='' before the flag loop; add 'val:filter_priority:--priority' to the parse_opts call
Add validate_priority call: if [[ -n "$filter_priority" ]]; then validate_priority "$filter_priority" || return 1; fi
Add priority filter to jq_filter: if [[ -n "$filter_priority" ]]; then jq_filter="$jq_filter | select((.priority // \"should\") == \"$filter_priority\")"; fi
Add --priority to the usage message and help text alongside --status and --type
Run shellcheck — confirm zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: aishore backlog list --priority must shows only must-priority items
aishore backlog list --priority should shows only should-priority items
aishore backlog list with no --priority still shows all items (backwards compatible)
aishore backlog list --priority invalid-value exits non-zero with an error message
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
